transcript:
Meeting Start: 2026-11-20 14:00 UTC
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Olivia Chen (Redwood AE), Rajiv Kumar (Redwood SE), Dr. Ana Morales, Jason Liu, Priya Shah (Meridian)

Summary (auto): Quick tour of the Redwood catalog and console. Demoed model shortlist, benchmark spreadsheet, and Optimize suggestions. Customer asked about data residency, latency budgets for 100 tps, and fallback policies for capacity. Agreed actions to run a pilot bench on two prompt families.

[00:00] Olivia Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Olivia with Redwood, and Rajiv will run through the console and the model catalog playbook.
[00:12] Dr. Ana Morales: Hi, Ana here. Thanks, Olivia. We're looking at options for clinical summarization — medium-length notes, some PII, so compliance and latency are both important.
[00:25] Jason Liu: Jason — platform side. We need to understand deployment choices: hosted API vs dedicated vs private in our cloud VPC.
[00:34] Olivia Chen: Great. Quick agenda — catalog filtering, how we interpret benchmarks, Optimize tuning (batching/quant), and then a short pilot plan. We'll drop links to the deck and bench sheet in chat.
[00:45] Rajiv Kumar: Opening the console now — apologies if screen flickers. So this is the model catalog view, we can filter by architecture, license, tokenization, and safety tags. For Meridian, I'd recommend starting with two open models: a mid-size RLHF-ish LLM and a smaller quantized model for throughput.
[01:12] Dr. Ana Morales: When you say "quantized model" — do you mean the 8-bit variants? Are there quality regressions we should expect?
[01:21] Rajiv Kumar: Good question. We surfaced quant profiles in Optimize — there's a small delta on long-context summarization beyond 1,500 tokens. For most clinical notes we see negligible drop at 4k context with our 8-bit Q4_K profiles; answer: yes slight perf delta but big cost wins. Note: transcription may say Q4K as "Q4 K" or 'q-four kay' — that's the kernel mapping shorthand.
[01:45] Jason Liu: Also curious about KV cache — you mentioned prefix-level caching previously, does that work with streaming API?
[01:53] Rajiv Kumar: Prefetch + KV cache works with streaming; we manage the cache on the runtime and it reduces repeated prompt overhead. There are heuristics in Optimize to suggest when to enable prefix caching vs full-session caching.
[02:12] [screen share] Olivia Chen: Pulling up the benchmark sheet — here's latency percentiles across models and hardware. You'll see columns for p50, p90, p95, tokens/s, and cost per 1k tokens. We've annotated rows where quantization maps to specific kernels (e.g., A100 fp16 -> fast-attn kernel, T4 -> fallback kernel with latency impact).
[02:42] Dr. Ana Morales: Hmm, on p95 we need <200ms for patient-facing UI. Your sheet shows p95 at 320ms for the mid-size model on the shared hosted tier. How much improvement with Dedicated?
[02:55] Rajiv Kumar: Dedicated reduces tail latency because of reserved GPUs and avoidance of noisy neighbors. For the same model on a dedicated A10 pool we've measured p95 around ~180-220ms depending on batch config. We can pin model version and set autoscaler policies to maintain SLO.
[03:18] Priya Shah: Security question — our legal team requires SOC2 and customer-managed KMS for keys. Can Redwood support HSM-backed KMS?
[03:27] Olivia Chen: Yes, for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS (HSM-A) and provide audit logs. For Hosted and Dedicated we offer KMS integration options; we'll surface SOC2 controls in the security pack we send.
[03:42] Jason Liu: For data residency, we need Europe region only. Is that a configuration or an additional contract?
[03:50] Rajiv Kumar: Region pinning is supported in both Dedicated and Private. Hosted API can be region-restricted but subject to capacity; Dedicated is the recommended route for strict residency. We'll note that in the pilot scope.
[04:05] [00:04:30] Olivia Chen: Quick demo of compatibility matrix — this is where we map model variants to kernel variants and hardware targets. The matrix shows recommended runtime kernels, quant support, and expected perf. If a kernel isn't available on a device we automatically route to a compatible variant — that's the graceful degradation flow.
[04:33] Dr. Ana Morales: Can you override routing? For example pin to a single kernel for reproducibility?
[04:40] Rajiv Kumar: Yes, you can lock routing policies per-route or per-tenant. We also support canary rollouts.
[04:51] Jason Liu: About the Optimize recommendations: how prescriptive are they? Will the console suggest batch sizes that might hurt latency?
[05:00] Rajiv Kumar: Optimize suggests batch sizes based on your target latency SLO and throughput. It gives tradeoffs (e.g., increase batch to 8 reduces cost per token by 18% but adds ~40ms p95). You can accept, edit, or pin suggestions. There's also a simulated cost impact column.
[05:22] [00:05:45] Priya Shah: Does Optimize keep historical config and alert if a rollout regresses quality? Our compliance team wants drift detection.
[05:31] Rajiv Kumar: We have quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets — you can upload your test prompts and set thresholds. If a new model or quant profile regresses we emit alerts and can auto-fallback to a safe variant.
[05:48] Dr. Ana Morales: For the pilot, what metrics should we expect to receive from Redwood? Token-level latency, error rates, token cost, and sample outputs for QA?
[05:58] Olivia Chen: Exactly — we'll provide per-request traces, token spend breakdown, p50/p95/p99 latency, and a small set of sample outputs with metadata for auditing. We'll also give a bench CSV you can drop into your own dashboards.
[06:14] Jason Liu: About integration: is the SDK language-friendly? We use Python services and some Node.js endpoints.
[06:21] Rajiv Kumar: SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. And a CLI if you want to run batch inference. The API supports streaming, function/tool calling, and structured output.
[06:33] [00:06:40] Olivia Chen: Going back to model selection — we recommend a two-track pilot: 1) mid-size open model with higher quality on Dedicated for interactive UI, 2) quantized small model for high-throughput batch summarization on Dedicated or Private. We'll measure quality delta, cost per 1k tokens, and latency tail.
[07:00] Dr. Ana Morales: For clinical safety & PII handling, do you support redaction pipelines or do we need to do that pre-inference?
[07:09] Rajiv Kumar: We recommend pre-inference redaction for PII, but we also can configure response filtering and have safety tags. For Private deployment we can run everything inside your VPC to reduce exfil risk.
[07:25] Priya Shah: Ok that helps. Also want to note our vendor review needs logs retained 1 year and SSO via SAML.
[07:32] Olivia Chen: Noted. SAML SSO is supported for console access; log retention is configurable as an add-on. We'll include that in the security pack.
[07:45] [00:07:50] Jason Liu: One more technical: under heavy load, what's the fallback policy? If Dedicated runs out of capacity can you route to a cheaper variant?
[07:55] Rajiv Kumar: We support policy-based routing: primary -> dedicated pool, fallback -> hosted compatible variant or lower-res model. Customers can set cost vs latency priorities. We'll show policy examples in the pilot config.
[08:13] Dr. Ana Morales: I noticed a column 'compatibility score' in the matrix — how is that calculated?
[08:20] Rajiv Kumar: It's a heuristic combining kernel-availability, memory fit, and quant-quality. It helps rank which model/hardware pair is likely to meet your SLOs. It's explainable — you can click to see why a model scored low.
[08:36] [00:08:45] Olivia Chen: Sharing the links here: deck: https://redwood.example/decks/meridian-catalog; benchmark sheet: https://redwood.example/bench/meridian-sample; pilot template: https://redwood.example/pilot/meridian-template.
[08:50] Priya Shah: I see the sheet, thanks. A small nit — I couldn't find the section on KMS integration details.
[08:58] Rajiv Kumar: That's in the security pack; I'll surface the specific KMS integration doc in the follow-up.
[09:05] Dr. Ana Morales: Can we run a small bench on our tokens — say 500 requests with two prompt families? Timeline?
[09:12] Olivia Chen: Yes, we can run that. Recommend week-of 2026-11-23 for the pilot; results in 48 hours after run completion. We'll need your prompts and a test service account.
[09:25] Jason Liu: For the bench run, do you need us to de-identify data? We might send synthetic prompts that mimic our distribution.
[09:33] Rajiv Kumar: Synthetic is perfect. We don't need real PHI. And for pilot telemetry we can do full logs inside your VPC if you choose Private.
[09:44] [00:10:00] Olivia Chen: Quick note on pricing — for a short Dedicated trial we can offer committed capacity with burst credits; I'll send a proposal. Pricing will show per-token estimates across variants and projected monthly spend.
[09:58] Priya Shah: And contract length? We prefer a 3-month evaluation for Dedicated.
[10:03] Olivia Chen: We can accommodate 3-month trial contracts.
[10:09] Dr. Ana Morales: Any notable limitations with long contexts ~8k tokens?
[10:15] Rajiv Kumar: Long-context is supported on certain model families and hardware — the matrix flags devices that can handle >8k efficiently. For some older kernels we fall back to chunking which impacts latency. We'll recommend models that have native long-context support.
[10:30] Jason Liu: One last thing — does Redwood provide model version pinning in the API so we can have reproducible outputs?
[10:36] Rajiv Kumar: Yes, model version pinning is first-class; rollouts allow canary and A/B tests. You can also pin quant profile and kernel selection if you want strict reproducibility.
[10:50] [00:11:00] Olivia Chen: We're nearing time — quick recap and next steps. We'll run a pilot on two prompt families week of 11/23, Rajiv will provision console access, Olivia will send pricing and security pack, Priya and Ana will share prompts and compliance questions. Follow-up call to review pilot results week of 11/30.
[11:18] Dr. Ana Morales: Sounds good. Thanks for the thorough walkthrough.
[11:22] Jason Liu: Thanks, helpful.
[11:24] Priya Shah: Thank you.
[11:28] Olivia Chen: Great, we'll follow up via email with links and dates.

Meeting End: 2026-11-20 14:49 UTC

Notes on transcription: Some technical terms may be mistranscribed (e.g., Q4_K sometimes appears as 'q four kay', KV cache as 'K V cash', and kernel names abbreviated). Speaker labels best-effort; timestamps are approximate.
